title: Section diagram of completed pullback on every K-flat representative
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On the small pro-etale site put $R_s=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_s$ and use unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\Gamma$ for exact final-object sections, regarded as an $\mathcal O_E$-module functor [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. For a strict tower $Z$ with transitions $t_n$, use
$$H(Z)^i=\prod_nZ_n^{i-1}\oplus\prod_nZ_n^i,\qquad d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_Z)a,da),\qquad s_Z((z_n))=(t_nz_{n+1}),$$
and diagonal product maps on strict tower morphisms [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. The symbol $c_Z:\Gamma H(Z)\to H(\Gamma Z)$ means the canonical product comparison on both displayed coordinates, not a chosen filler of a triangle.

Let $Y$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible and $f:s\to Y$ a scheme morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Put $R_Y=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_Y$. For arbitrary $K\in D(R_Y)$ and a flat-term K-flat representative $q:P\to K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], put
$$P_n=P\otimes_{R_Y}(A_n)_Y,\qquad C_f(P)_n=\operatorname{Res}_nf_n^*P_n,\qquad B_f(P)_n=\Gamma C_f(P)_n,$$
with actual quotient transitions. Here $f_n^*$ is the exact finite module inverse image with the canonical coefficient-ring identification, and $\operatorname{Res}_n$ restricts along $R_s\to(A_n)_s$ [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $\mathsf P_f$ be the ambient completed pullback functor defined by the strict quotient-cone construction [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], and let $\jmath_{f,K,P,q}:\mathsf P_fK\xrightarrow{\sim}H(C_f(P))$ be its specified representative comparison [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined].

The strict tower $C_f(P)$, not merely its separate levels, computes the finite derived pullbacks $\operatorname{Res}_nLf_n^*(K\otimes^L_{R_Y}(A_n)_Y)$ and their coefficient quotient maps. The canonical chain map
$$c_{C_f(P)}:\Gamma H(C_f(P))\xrightarrow{\sim}H(B_f(P))$$
is an isomorphism, with identity on both sectionwise product components in the displayed coordinates. The chain functor $P\mapsto H(B_f(P))$ sends quasi-isomorphisms between flat-term K-flat complexes to quasi-isomorphisms, and hence descends after localization. There are derived representative comparisons
$$v_{f,K,P,q}=c_{C_f(P)}\Gamma(\jmath_{f,K,P,q}):\Gamma\mathsf P_fK\xrightarrow{\sim}H(B_f(P)).$$
For every chain map $u:P\to P'$ and derived map $h:K\to K'$ satisfying $q'u=hq$ after localization, the representative of $\Gamma\mathsf P_f(h)$ under these same comparisons is the diagonal cone map $[H((\Gamma\operatorname{Res}_nf_n^*(u\otimes1))_n)]$. This equality holds also for inverse quasi-isomorphisms and composites of roofs; hence the comparisons are natural for all derived morphisms and independent of the chosen flat-term K-flat representative under its specified comparison maps. The target $H(B_f(P))$ is a derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit] of the entire evaluated finite-pullback tower. Neither a choice of unrelated levelwise isomorphisms nor an arbitrary isomorphism of Roos triangles enters. No completeness, constructibility or boundedness of $K$, and no invertibility of $f$, is assumed.

proof.text: Use scalarRoosMap_existsUnique, the existing additive comparison normalized on both mapping-cocone coordinates and all product projections. Sections are evaluation followed by restriction of scalars, hence preserve countable products. In each degree identify the cocone with its two summands using the canonical cocone coordinate isomorphism. The matrix of scalarRoosMap is the direct sum of the two product comparisons, which are isomorphisms. Thus it is a chain isomorphism. Convert the first coordinate equation into an equation in every degree and specialize the second to j=i-1. Conversely the given coordinate equations recover the full normalization; uniqueness of scalarRoosMap and Iso.ext give the required unique isomorphism. podReindexingRoosNaturality proves strict naturality of these maps, and uniqueness identifies the chosen sectionRoosComparison with the same map.

proof.text: Compose the specified integralDerivedPullbackComparison, the exact derived-sections factorization, and the natural Roos comparison from step 2. This gives a natural isomorphism e on the whole good representative category. Its component is exactly representative with q=identity. For arbitrary q, the definition of representative is completedSections(q inverse) followed by e at P. Naturality of e and the equation Q(u) q prime = q h now give the representative diagram by functoriality and cancellation. For a quasi-isomorphism u, completedSections(Q(u)) is invertible; this naturality square and the isomorphisms e imply invertibility of moduleQ(sectionRoos(u)). Localization reflects quasi-isomorphisms, proving hInv without a separate homotopy calculation.

proof.text: For the displayed roof equation, apply the chain-map diagram to both legs with source representative (W,identity). Precompose the required equality by completedSections(Q(a) q). This is an isomorphism. Substitute the specified formula for h, cancel Q(a) and q, use the two chain-map diagrams, and cancel moduleQ(sectionRoos(a)). For existence of a good roof, Mathlib DerivedCategory.right_fac gives a chain roof P <- Z -> P prime using the right calculus of fractions. Resolve Z by a K-flat complex W with flat terms. The canonical site-tensor comparison converts flatness of the tensor-right functor to IsFlatOnSite, so W is good. Compose both roof legs with the resolution map r. The left leg remains a quasi-isomorphism and Q(r) cancels in the fraction formula.

proof.text: Apply the already proved generic roos_derivedLimit from the well-definedness module to the entire sectionTower(P), in the ordinary module category with its standard localization. Exact countable products identify the localized product complexes with products in the derived category, via derivedCategory_countableProducts_core. Transport the localized distinguished mapping-cocone triangle along these product comparisons. Product projections identify its middle map with precisely 1 minus the shift for the actual localized transitions. This proves IsDerivedLimit for moduleQ(sectionRoos(P)) without constructing a total derived inverse-limit functor or choosing a triangle filler.
